# Cartesia — calls, statuses, transcripts, pagination

Primary source: `cartesia-ai/cartesia-python`, `src/cartesia/resources/agents/calls.py`,
`src/cartesia/types/agents/agent_call.py`, `src/cartesia/types/agents/agent_transcript.py`,
`src/cartesia/types/agents/call_list_params.py`, `src/cartesia/pagination.py`.
Cross-checked against `cartesia-js/src/resources/agents/calls.ts`.

## Call endpoints in the official clients

| Method | Path | Source | Standing |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/agents/calls/{call_id}` | `calls.py:73` | VERIFIED-SDK |
| GET | `/agents/calls` | `calls.py:122` | VERIFIED-SDK |
| GET | `/agents/calls/{call_id}/audio` | `calls.py:172` | VERIFIED-SDK |
| POST | `/agents/calls` — place outbound calls | outbound-dialing docs page | **REPORTED-DOCS only.** Absent from both generated clients. |
| POST | `/agents/calls/{id}/end` | nothing | **Invented by us.** No source anywhere. |

The reported outbound shape, for the record (REPORTED-DOCS, `docs.cartesia.ai/line/integrations/telephony/outbound-dialing`):
`POST https://api.cartesia.ai/agents/calls` with `from_number_id`, `agent_id`,
`ringing_timeout_seconds` and an `outbound_calls: [{to_number, metadata}]` array,
returning one `agent_call_id` per number. The snippet adds that *"the `from_number_id`
can be any phone number on your account; it does not need to be assigned to an agent"* —
which is why the adapter refuses to dial without one rather than guessing.

## `AgentCall` — what a call actually looks like

`types/agents/agent_call.py` (VERIFIED-SDK):

| Field | Type | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | str | **the call id — not `agent_call_id`** |
| `agent_id` | str | |
| `status` | `Literal["active","completed","failed","cancelled"]` | the entire vocabulary |
| `deployment_id` | str? | |
| `start_time` | datetime? | **not `started_at`/`created_at`** |
| `end_time` | datetime? | **not `ended_at`** |
| `error_message` | str? | |
| `summary` | str? | *"a brief summary of the call that is generated by Cartesia"* |
| `telephony_params` | `{from, to}`? | **nested**, not top level. Documented as `from` = "The phone number of the agent", `to` = "The phone number of the caller". |
| `transcript` | `[AgentTranscript]`? | only present when asked for — see pagination |

**Absent**: any duration field, any recording URL, any cost or currency, any `direction`.
Audio is fetched separately from `/agents/calls/{call_id}/audio`, which needs the API key,
so it is not a URL a downstream fetcher can be handed the way Bolna's signed S3 link is.

### Status mapping

| Cartesia | ours | terminal? |
|---|---|---|
| `active` | `in_progress` | no |
| `completed` | `completed` | yes |
| `failed` | `failed` | yes |
| `cancelled` | `failed` | **yes** |

`cancelled` has no equivalent in `calevate_shared.events.CallStatus`, and `failed` is the
right landing place: it is terminal and it is not billable-as-success. The defect this
finding closed was not the mapping (an unmapped status already degraded to `failed`) but
the TERMINALITY — `cancelled` was not in `_TERMINAL_RAW`, so a cancelled call stayed
non-terminal for ever, was re-polled on every reconciliation tick, and never reached the
post-call pipeline.

`queued`/`ringing`/`no_answer`/`busy`/`voicemail` are **not** in Cartesia's enum. The
adapter still maps them, which costs nothing and covers the case where the enum grows.

### `telephony_params.from` / `.to`, and a question we are NOT answering

Cartesia documents `from` as the agent's number and `to` as the caller's number. On an
outbound call that matches our `from_e164`/`to_e164` exactly. On an INBOUND call, read
literally, it is the reverse of ours. Nothing sourced says whether the field meanings flip
with direction, and there is no `direction` field to key off. The adapter therefore maps
them straight through and does not invent a swap; settling it is OPERATIONS §2 gate 16(d).

## `AgentTranscript` — the transcript entry

`types/agents/agent_transcript.py` (VERIFIED-SDK):

| Field | Type | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | str | *"Roles are `user`, `assistant`, or `system`. `assistant` is the agent. `system` is used to indicate logs during the conversation such as `log_event` or `log_metric`."* |
| `text` | str? | **the utterance — not `content`** |
| `start_timestamp`, `end_timestamp` | float | seconds relative to call start |
| `end_reason` | str? | `call_ended` / `interrupted` / `tts_completed` |
| `text_chunks` | `[{start_timestamp, text}]`? | finer-grained |
| `tool_calls` | `[{id, name, arguments}]`? | |
| `log_event` | `{event, metadata, timestamp}`? | |
| `log_metric` | `{name, value, timestamp}`? | |
| `tts_ttfb`, `vad_buffer_ms` | float?, int? | |

Two defects this closed: the adapter read `content` (never populated, so **every** real
transcript parsed to zero turns and reported them all as unparsed), and it mapped every
non-agent role to `caller` — so a `system` row, which is a LOG entry and not speech at
all, would have been written into a client's transcript as something the caller said.
`system` rows are now skipped and are not counted as unparsed, because they are not
utterances we failed to read.

## Pagination and filtering — `GET /agents/calls`

`types/agents/call_list_params.py` and the method docstring at `calls.py:95-98`
(VERIFIED-SDK):

> *"Lists calls sorted by start time in descending order for a specific agent. `agent_id`
> is required and if you want to include `transcript` in the response, add
> `expand=transcript` to the request. This endpoint is paginated."*

| Param | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `agent_id` | **yes** | `Required[str]` in the TypedDict |
| `limit` | no | 1–100 per page |
| `starting_after` | no | cursor: the id of the call to start after |
| `ending_before` | no | cursor: the id of the call to end before |
| `expand` | no | only supported value is `transcript` |

Envelope: `SyncCursorIDPage[AgentCall]` → `{"data": [...]}` (`pagination.py:49-57`). There
is **no `has_more`**: `next_page_info` derives the next cursor from the last item's id
(`pagination.py:60-73`), so "was that the last page?" is only answerable by asking again.

**There is no time filter.** No `since`, `created_after`, `start_time` or equivalent. The
adapter's previous `params={"start_time": …}` was invented, and its lack of `agent_id`
would have made every listing a 4xx.

Consequences for `VoiceEngine.list_executions(since=…)`, which is global and time-bounded:

1. it must fan out over `GET /agents` (`{"summaries": [...]}`) to obtain agent ids;
2. it must page each agent with `limit`/`starting_after`;
3. it must ask for `expand=transcript` or get no transcripts at all;
4. it must apply `since` client-side — cheaply, because the order is start-time DESC, so
   the walk for an agent can stop at the first row older than `since`.
